issue.title: Close button on notifications is read as "Dismiss" in French
issue.body:
One of our accountants uses VoiceOver with her Ledgerline profile set to French.
The text of the small notifications at the bottom of the page is read in French
("Fichier reçu. L'import va bientôt commencer."), but the close button on every
notification is announced as "Dismiss, button". The upload form and the date
range picker around it are read in French too.
## Discussion

### ben-ops (maintainer) · 2026-11-05
Thanks for the report. Is it every notification, or only the one after an upload?

### a11y-review-cm · 2026-11-05
Every one we've seen. The button looks the same (×); it's only what the
screen reader says.

input.title: Translate the toast close button's aria-label with the user's locale
input.body:
File: src/components/Toast.tsx

The close button's aria-label is built with t("ui.toast.dismiss") and no locale argument, so it always falls back to DEFAULT_LOCALE ("en") and screen readers announce "Dismiss" for French users, although src/i18n/fr.json defines "Fermer" for that key. Change the Toast component and its provider to accept the active locale (as DateRangePicker and ReportTable already do) and pass it as t("ui.toast.dismiss", {}, locale). The provider's caller should supply the locale from the user's profile.

Thanks for the detailed report; here is what triage found.

The notification close button's aria-label is set with t("ui.toast.dismiss") and no locale, so it always resolves to the English "Dismiss", even though fr.json has "Fermer" for that key. The other components pass their locale through; Toast does not. A draft pull request (pr-27) proposes passing the active locale into the toast component.

In short: the notification close button's aria-label is set with t("ui.toast.dismiss") and no locale, so it always resolves to the English "Dismiss", even though fr.json has "Fermer" for that key.
